BADGER METER, INC.
Badger Meter, Inc. introduced OneNetwork, a real-time network monitoring and analysis platform providing water distribution, wastewater collection and stormwater system managers with a unified, real-time view of their diverse network asset and sensor data. The announcement comes during WEFTEC, the annual water event, hosted this year in New Orleans, Louisiana. OneNetwork extends the value of software and analytics offered by Badger Meter by further connecting the BlueEdge® portfolio, the suite of smart water management solutions, water technology, software and services for continuous water management.
OneNetwork builds upon the company?s success and adds to its software solutions which have been purpose-built for the modern needs of the water industry. OneNetwork helps utilities understand the health and performance of their networks to see clearer, act faster and manage smarter. Water and wastewater utilities manage highly diverse infrastructure using SCADA systems, GIS platforms and point sensors that rarely talk to one another.
That fragmentation slows response to network events, including main breaks, water quality and pressure anomalies. To enable targeted operational response and prioritize capital investment where it matters most, connected data is necessary. OneNetwork delivers network visibility and connectedness through: Industry-leading connection with AMI, unlocking the full operational value of an investment in smart metering.
A single operational view across network data sources, with reduced time spent switching between systems. Improved situational awareness with real-time event alerts and advanced analytics with built-in support workflows for managing main breaks, water quality events, pressure transients and non-revenue-water spikes. Interactive functionality with GIS-based alarm indicators and details with a live map for a real-time view of the entire distribution or collection network. Centralized alarm reporting with contextual chart overlays for alarm severity and the ability to view details down to the individual site and asset level.
Powerful filtering to quickly locate relevant assets by pipe material, age, size, valve type and repair history. Enhanced field and labor efficiency, realized by turning static asset records into operational tools for improved asset monitoring and management. The presentation, titled ?Zero Blind Spots: OneNetwork?A New Approach to Network Visibility?
will introduce OneNetwork with a walk through of the software in action, including compelling use cases that exhibit the unique value of OneNetwork and demonstrates the difference between OneNetwork and other systems. OneNetwork will first be available to North American water and wastewater utilities starting September 2026, with plans to expand the offering globally soon.

As the Q2 earnings season comes to a close, it's time to take stock of this quarter's best and worst performers in the inspection instruments industry, including Badger Meter (NYSE:BMI) and its peers.
Measurement and inspection instrument companies may enjoy more steady demand because products such as water meters are non-discretionary and mandated for replacement at predictable intervals. In the last decade, digitization and data collection have driven innovation in the space, leading to incremental sales. But like the broader industrials sector, measurement and inspection instrument companies are at the whim of economic cycles. Interest rates, for example, can greatly impact civil, commercial, and residential construction projects that drive demand.
The 5 inspection instruments stocks we track reported a very strong Q2. As a group, revenues beat analysts' consensus estimates by 2.6% while next quarter's revenue guidance was 2.5% above.

The developer of the world's first frost-proof water meter in 1905, Badger Meter (NYSE:BMI) provides water control and measure equipment to various industries.

The market seems disappointed with the results as the stock is down 15.1% since reporting and currently trades at $123.89.
